clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old female presented with 10 months of left-sided pulsatile tinnitus (PT). Initial CT and MRA suggested a dural arteriovenous fistula (DAVF) in the lesser sphenoid wing and left para-cavernous sinus regions, with efferent drainage to the superior ophthalmic vein (SOV), inferior ophthalmic vein (IOV), and pterygoid plexus. Ocular assessments and physical examination were unremarkable. The patient declined invasive diagnostics (DSA) and opted for conservative observation. After 30 months, the pulsatile tinnitus spontaneously ceased. Follow-up MRAs at 30 and 42 months confirmed the spontaneous closure of the DAVF, with no residual radiological indications of the fistula or recurrence of PT. Throughout the clinical course, PT remained the sole symptom, with no reported ocular symptoms or other neurological deficits.
